task:
COLONY PLANNER S4c FOLLOW-UP ON BRANCH plan/s4c-layout: IN THE SYSTEM PANE, SHOW EACH SITE ON ITS OWN LINE WITH ITS STATION NAME FIRST, AND SEPARATE ORBITAL FROM SURFACE SITES CLEARLY. CHANGE ONLY apps/web/src/lib/features/plan/ (SystemPane.svelte, PlanIcon.svelte, plan.css and their tests), plus apps/web/cypress/e2e/plan.cy.ts only where a selector moved. NO MODEL, STORAGE, API OR DEPENDENCY CHANGES. KEEP EVERYTHING THE PREVIOUS COMMIT ON THIS BRANCH ADDED.

Owner feedback (2026-10-31), comparing with Raven Colonial's system view:
- the station names must be shown the way Raven shows them;
- it is not obvious which sites are on the ground and which are in orbit.

Today `SystemPane.svelte`'s `tiles` snippet renders every site of a body as wrapping chips: number, status, facility type, then the name in small text. Orbital and surface sites are mixed together.

1. Two groups under each body. Below each body row, render the body's sites as two groups, in this order, each only when it has sites:
   - **Orbital**: a small muted heading "Orbital" with an orbit icon (a dotted circle, inline SVG) before the word.
   - **Surface**: a small muted heading "Surface" with a globe icon (inline SVG) before the word, inside a lightly shaded box (a subtle background token that works in light and dark themes) indented under the body, like Raven's grey surface box.
   - Each group is a `<ul>` with an accessible name, for example `aria-label="Orbital sites on <body short name>"` and `aria-label="Surface sites on <body short name>"`.
   - The grouping uses `site.slot_kind`. Add the two icons to `PlanIcon.svelte` as kinds `orbital` and `surface`, `aria-hidden`; the group heading text carries the meaning, so nothing is colour-only.
   - The Unplaced list is grouped the same way.
2. One line per site, name first. Each site is one `<li>` containing the existing button (it still opens Why), laid out as:
   - step number, with ★ for the first site as now;
   - status icon;
   - the station name in a prominent weight. With no name, use the facility type here and omit the next item;
   - the facility type in muted text, for example "Communication Installation" or "Industrial Surface Outpost";
   - tier chip;
   - the result icon for planned steps.
   Long names wrap onto a second line inside the item rather than being cut off. There is no ellipsis truncation on the name (the facility type may still truncate with an ellipsis and a `title`).
3. Accessible name of each site button: "Step N, Primary Port (when first), <status>, <name>, <facility type>, <orbital|surface>, <result when planned>". This replaces the current order. Keep the `title` tooltip with the full text.
4. The header toggle stays, but its labels become "Names and types" (pressed) and "Types only". In "Types only", the line shows the facility type in the name position and hides the name.
5. Keep the compact feel. Each site line is about 24–28 px tall, the group headings are about 16 px, and there are no extra borders between bodies. No horizontal page scroll at 390 px. Existing slot chips, the body row, the "+" button and the facility picker do not change.

TESTS (component tests, existing conventions):
- A body with two orbital and one surface site renders an "Orbital" group with 2 items and a "Surface" group with 1 item, in that order, with the accessible names above.
- A body with only surface sites renders no Orbital group.
- A site's line shows the name before the facility type, and with no name only the facility type.
- "Types only" hides names.
- The first site's button accessible name starts "Step 1, Primary Port".
- Unplaced sites are grouped the same way.
- Update the existing compact-layout test (`CompactLayout.test.ts`) to the new structure without weakening what it checks: one row per body heading, and each site on a single compact line.

VALIDATION: in apps/web: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test` (report counts), `pnpm build`. SUMMARY: the files changed and the new markup structure of a body's site groups.
